skill.name: get-my-team-posting
skill.description: Turn one company message into posts each colleague can publish in their own words, instead of six people posting the same paragraph. Use when a company wants employees posting, a launch needs internal support, or a team was handed copy to share. Do not write one post for everyone to paste, do not write in a voice they would not recognise, and never ask anyone to post what they disagree with.
skill.summary: Create distinct employee posts from one approved company message while preserving each person's voice and choice.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Turn One Company Message Into Team Posts
content.value_statement: Teams often publish identical employee posts that feel scripted and weaken trust. This skill turns one approved message into distinct drafts based on each person's experience, voice, and willingness to share.
actual_capabilities: Separate an approved company message from individual employee posts.
Identify personal angles based on each person's work or direct experience.
Adapt drafts to examples of an employee's existing writing.
Recommend staggered publishing across different days and normal posting times.
Flag uncleared customer details, metrics, and roadmap claims before publication.
Support voluntary participation and approval by the named employee.
limitations: It does not publish posts or manage social media accounts.
It cannot verify claims, customer permissions, or company approvals.
It needs genuine employee examples to match an individual voice.
VoiceMOAT features require an external connector and eligible plan.

use_cases.title: Launch Advocacy
use_cases.description: Create varied employee drafts for a product launch while keeping the approved message accurate and voluntary.

use_cases.title: Expert-Led Sharing
use_cases.description: Turn engineering, support, or sales experience into personal posts that add useful evidence to a company announcement.

use_cases.title: Executive Review
use_cases.description: Prepare distinct drafts for leaders and subject experts, then route each draft to its named author for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Team Drafts
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this approved company message into three distinct employee post ideas. Ask for each person's real experience before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Match Personal Voices
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one draft for each teammate using their role, direct experience, and two writing samples. Keep the shared message accurate.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Staggered Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a voluntary posting plan across five days. Give each person a different angle, a suitable time, and a clear approval step.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Advocacy Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these employee drafts for repeated wording, unsupported claims, brand-voice imitation, missing approvals, and pressure to publish. Recommend precise revisions.

output_examples.input: Company message: We reduced report setup time. Maya is a support lead who helped test the workflow.
output_examples.output: Maya's draft: I tested the new report setup with our support team. The clearest improvement was finding the right starting point faster, especially during busy customer calls.

output_examples.input: Company message: Our new feature is available. Devon joined the project after early customer feedback.
output: Angle: What changed after customer feedback.
Draft direction: Explain the problem customers raised, the adjustment made, and one limitation that remains.

best_practices: Confirm the shared message before creating individual drafts.
Use direct experience and real writing samples as the basis for each voice.
Give every named employee time to approve, edit, or decline their draft.
anti_patterns: Sending one identical post to every employee.
Inventing personal experiences or writing in a voice the author has not approved.
Publishing uncleared customer details, metrics, or roadmap claims.

faq.question: Does this create one post for everyone?
faq.answer: No. It creates distinct drafts only when each person has a relevant experience to share.

faq.question: Can employees decline to post?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow treats declining as a valid outcome and does not require participation.

faq.question: How does it match a person's voice?
faq.answer: It uses the person's role, direct experience, and examples of their existing writing.

faq.question: Does it publish to social platforms?
faq.answer: No. It prepares drafts and review guidance. A person must approve and publish each post.

faq.question: Can it use VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes VoiceMOAT profile and scoring functions when the connector and plan support them.

faq.question: What should be reviewed before posting?
faq.answer: Check factual accuracy, permissions, confidential information, personal approval, and any company link guidance.
